title: Pflege-TÜV declared failed
what_happened: Greens called Pflege-TÜV a failure: undifferentiated grades, focus on documentation, no consumer-protection value; demanded independent institute.
lesson: Interpretation: Criteria designed by providers/payers rather than users attract long-running criticism; involve user/patient perspective.

title: Stiftung Warentest introduces paid logo licence
what_happened: From 01.07.2013 advertising with test results requires a paid logo licence via RAL; food industry criticised cost and undifferentiated fee structure.
lesson: Interpretation: Even the most trusted tester monetises seals; fee structure should vary by sector/entity size to avoid backlash.

title: BGH VI ZR 358/13 Jameda listing permissible
what_happened: Listing doctors with patient ratings without consent is generally permissible when the portal acts as neutral information intermediary.
lesson: Interpretation: Building master lists of professionals from public data is legally feasible, if neutrality is kept.

title: Kaufland seal over untested products
what_happened: BGH confirmed that showing a 'Gut' logo over several products when only one was tested is impermissible.
lesson: Interpretation: Seal misuse by licensees (e.g., group-wide use for one listed location) creates liability and reputational risk; licence monitoring needed (RAL model).

title: LTO critique of FOCUS Top-Anwälte
what_happened: Peer recommendations (1.6 per respondent) without editorial correction; only 33 of top-50 overlap JUVE; sympathy/rivalry effects.
lesson: Interpretation: Peer-survey lists in professional services need minimum response thresholds and plausibility checks against market data.

title: BGH VI ZR 30/17 Jameda neutrality lost
what_happened: Jameda lost neutral status because premium (paying) doctors were shielded from competitor ads displayed on non-paying doctors' profiles; plaintiff's profile had to be deleted. Jameda removed the feature immediately.
lesson: Interpretation: Any visible advantage for paying (seal-licensing) entities in a list/portal can destroy the neutrality defence; separate editorial ranking from paid presentation.

title: Burda seal business double-digit millions
what_happened: Burda reorganised FOCUS line extensions and created a Center of Competence for seal consulting, research and sales from 01.06.2018; CEO stated seal business generates double-digit million euro revenue with strong margins.
lesson: Interpretation: Seal licensing is the core revenue driver; topic potential should be scored on number of licensable entities and their marketing budgets.

title: Pflegenoten (Pflege-TÜV) abolished
what_happened: School-grade Pflegenoten replaced from autumn 2019 by indicator-based quality system; average grade had been 1.2 across >13,000 facilities, so grades did not differentiate.
lesson: Interpretation: A rating where nearly everyone scores 'very good' loses credibility; a TOP list must ensure real dispersion and that bad results cannot be compensated by good ones in unrelated areas.

title: EuGH ÖKO-TEST seal trademark
what_happened: EuGH: testers can prohibit seal use only where the seal is a reputed trademark and use is misleading; mere registration insufficient. ÖKO-TEST licenses seal per specific tested product with current result.
lesson: Interpretation: Brand reputation of the seal is a legal asset; enforcement against unlicensed use depends on seal reputation.

title: BGH 2021 Jameda premium profiles allowed (dentists)
what_happened: BGH dismissed deletion claims of two NRW dentists: no general right to equal treatment of free vs premium profiles; neutrality lost only with hidden advantages for paying customers.
lesson: Interpretation: Paid add-ons are tolerable if they do not affect ranking or visibility of competitors in a hidden way.

title: BGH I ZR 134/20 OBI 'Testsieger' without source
what_happened: Advertising with Stiftung Warentest 'Testsieger' seal without stating issue/year of test is misleading by omission (§5a UWG).
lesson: Interpretation: Seal licence terms should require licensees to cite edition/year and source, protecting both list and licensee.

title: BILANZ disclaimer on peer-based lawyer ranking
what_happened: Publisher explicitly states its peer-based list is not a quality assessment and reflects subjective views; small firms may be underrepresented.
lesson: Interpretation: Explicitly framing lists as 'recommendations' with stated limits matches what the BGH now requires on health seals.

title: Newsweek/Statista World's Best Hospitals critique
what_happened: Ranking based on survey of 80,000 professionals; reputation >50% weight; 19 of 27 countries lacked patient-experience data and 13 lacked quality measures; cross-country comparison not meaningful.
lesson: Interpretation: Reputation-heavy methods are cheap but criticised; blend with hard outcome data where available.

title: Publisher's 'Wildwuchs' argument and JUVE distinction
actor: LG München I (as reported by MIR)
what_happened: Publisher argued its seals answered a 'Wildwuchs' of seals; court distinguished the BVerfG 'Juve-Handbuch' case (ad-financed directory) from paid seals sold to rated subjects.
lesson: Interpretation: Ad-financed editorial lists enjoy stronger press-law protection than lists whose revenue comes from the rated entities; consider hybrid revenue models.

title: LG München I 4 HK O 14545/21 FOCUS doctor seals
actor: Wettbewerbszentrale vs Burda publisher (FOCUS-Gesundheit); LG München I, 4. Kammer für Handelssachen
what_happened: Court enjoined awarding/publishing 'TOP Mediziner' and 'FOCUS Empfehlung' seals (licence ~EUR 2,000 net) as misleading: seals resemble neutral test marks while criteria (peer recommendations, patient satisfaction) are subjective; press freedom did not cover paid seal licensing.
lesson: Interpretation: For any new health-related list, the paid seal is the legal attack surface, not the editorial list; topic scoring should penalise topics where quality can only be measured subjectively.

title: Weisse Liste ended after ~18 years
what_happened: Bertelsmann Stiftung ended the Weisse Liste public-reporting project in 2024 after ~18 years despite ~1m monthly visitors in earlier years and licence deals with insurers; low uptake among office-based doctors had been noted.
lesson: Interpretation: Even well-funded, neutral comparison portals struggle with sustainable financing; reach alone does not secure a business model.

title: Bundes-Klinik-Atlas launch errors
what_happened: One week after launch (May 2024) DKG documented wrong case numbers (e.g., 4 instead of 156 prostatectomies; 6 instead of >75 preterm births) and wrong emergency levels.
lesson: Interpretation: Data errors in public rankings are immediately publicised by affected providers; verify case counts with providers before publication.

title: AWMF demands beta label for Klinik-Atlas
what_happened: Medical societies demanded atlas be labelled beta: incomplete, unchecked data, mixing of diagnoses, regional coding differences, no version history.
lesson: Interpretation: Expert societies are veto players for health rankings; consult them early.

title: DKI survey: 79% of hospitals found errors
what_happened: Of 412 general hospitals surveyed, 79% reported incorrect information in the Klinik-Atlas.
lesson: Interpretation: Feedback/correction loop with listed entities is essential quality control.

title: OLG München 29 U 867/23 e reversal
what_happened: Appeal court reversed LG: consumers understand seals as editorial recommendation, FOCUS logo shows sender, objective elements (training, publications, memberships) also used; revision not admitted.
lesson: Interpretation: Legal risk is volatile across instances; a scout should not treat a favourable ruling as settled.

title: Bundes-Klinik-Atlas wound down
what_happened: Project group dissolved retroactively to 30.06.2025; atlas cost ~EUR 1.5m/yr vs ~EUR 120k for the DKG directory; DKG claims 600,000 vs 200,000 monthly visits.
lesson: Interpretation: State transparency tools can disappear, leaving orientation gaps that media lists fill - but also showing that hospital transparency is politically contested.

title: FOCUS Klinikliste: private clinics not comparable
what_happened: Private clinics are listed separately because they lack mandatory quality reports, so direct comparison is impossible.
lesson: Interpretation: Data availability asymmetries within a segment force separate lists; check whether every entity type in a new topic has comparable public data.

title: New care quality system too complex for consumers
what_happened: Indicator-based quality presentation (inpatient since 2019, ambulatory since 01.07.2026) is more precise but more complex; vdek says it is not yet usable at a glance.
lesson: Interpretation: Gap between precise official data and consumer usability = orientation opportunity (e.g., ambulatory care services) - but must translate data faithfully.

title: Pay-to-play employer seals under scrutiny
what_happened: Commentary names pay-to-play awards (granted essentially for a fee without objective check) as risk in EmpCo context.
lesson: Interpretation: Keep listing free and separate from licence sale (as FOCUS states for Klinikliste) and communicate it.

title: FOCUS Pflegeheime: caveat on measurability
what_happened: Editors note care quality cannot be fully measured and unlisted homes are not implicitly worse; method combines self-reports with MD inspection reports.
lesson: Interpretation: After BGH I ZR 130/25, heavy reliance on self-reports is a legal weak spot; public MD reports are a stronger anchor for care topics.

title: BGH I ZR 130/25 strict standards for health test seals
what_happened: BGH set aside OLG and remanded: seals are health-related test logos requiring strict accuracy; limitations of the method must be visible on the seal; unclear pool admission, point allocation, reliance on doctors' self-reports and previous award as sole inclusion criterion were not examined; paid seal provision is a commercial practice under UWG, list publication is press activity.
lesson: Interpretation: New health/care TOP lists need documented, disclosed criteria and weights, limited reliance on self-reports, and seal designs that state basis (e.g. 'peer recommendation'). Topics with objective public data (e.g. MD reports, quality reports) score better.

title: BGH ruling transparency critique (AOK commentary)
what_happened: Commentary highlights that the court could not reliably tell how awarded doctors differed from non-awarded ones, and that criteria/weights and data-quality checks were not disclosed.
lesson: Interpretation: Publish a methodology dossier with weights and quality checks before launch; payers (AOK) watch health seals critically.

title: EmpCo / UWG: sustainability labels need certification
actor: Bundestag (Drittes Gesetz zur Änderung des UWG, implementing EU 2024/825)
what_happened: From 27.09.2026 sustainability labels are only allowed if based on an independent certification scheme or established by public authorities; §15b UWG transitional rule for goods already on market until 27.09.2028.
lesson: Interpretation: Any 'sustainable provider' TOP list/seal (e.g. green craftsmen, sustainable employers) faces higher legal bar; avoid sustainability-claim seals unless certification-based.
